what:
At Beaufort, from the ebb down to dead low, the marsh grass now stands on its bank. Along the top of both near banks (the oak's bank on the left, the dock and palmetto bank on the right) there is now a band of wet, dark mud between the grass and the river. The grass's feet are in a darker wet strip at the bottom of it, and a few pale bits of dead stem (wrack) lie there. On Josh's morning (tide 0.15) the band is about 7 to 8 scene units tall on a 375 or 390 phone. Its top edge is inked like the flats, with a thin wet shine, and it rises and dips a little along the bank instead of being a ruled line.

At each bank's corner by the channel, the mud carries on under the tall grass and slopes down into the flat in the flat's own colour. The tall corner grass now stands on that mud. Before, it had the river showing between its feet, and on a rising tide it stood over open water. Under the dock walkway the mud stays a sliver below the walkway, so the walkway still reads as standing above the marsh.

The band follows the tide on the same curve as the flats. It is fullest at dead low, shrinks through mid tide to a thin strip at 0.8, and disappears at 0.94 and above. A spring high looks exactly as it did before, with the river up around the stems.

The flats keep their look and their tide behaviour. The only change to them is a small mud shoulder where each one meets its bank. The grass keeps its exact blades, positions and sway. The oak, its light and the sun are untouched. Nothing new moves.
how:
Why it read as floating: the spartina tufts (tuftRun) stand on the land shapes' top lines (landL, landR). Behind that line the page draws the river band (lcwaterband) at the same height at every tide. So at low water the grass's feet were seen against the river while the flats and the float showed the water was down. Separately, the tall corner runs (W*.25..lEdge+2 and rEdge-2..W*.79) reach past the land's corner. There the flat's top line drops as the tide rises, which left feet over open water: on main at tide 0.8, foot (238.0, 190.6) at 390 was over water on all three samples.

The tide gate: a new pure function, bftGrassMud(tide), next to bftDockWater. It uses bftDockTide, so an unknown tide counts as mid water. It returns 0 at BFT_GRASS_WET (0.94) and above, and BFT_GRASS_MUD*((0.94 - t)/0.94)^0.85 below that, with BFT_GRASS_MUD = 4. That is 4 units at dead low, 3.45 at 0.15, 2.1 at 0.5 and 0.79 at 0.8. Nothing new is drawn unless mudH > 0.05.

The geometry, inside lowcountryScene:
- BANKS records each bank's top line exactly as the land path draws it (two quadratics), its flat's top line and toe face, and which way the channel lies.
- The bank-mud path (grassBank) has a top edge that is a spline through 25 samples of the land's top line raised by mudH. The height varies by up to ±36% on a fixed mulberry seed (7741 left, 7753 right), evens out near the corner, and on the right is kept at least deckY+1.6 below the walkway.
- At the corner the top edge runs on for 3.6 units, then a cubic drops it into the flat's outline 6 to 9 units out, matching the outline's slope there (bezAt solves x by bisection; flatAt covers both the top line and the toe face).
- The fill's lower edge follows the flat's outline 0.7 units inside it, then runs under the land.
- Fill is a horizontal gradient (lcbank0, lcbank1) from dark wet mud to the flat's own mudC at the join, plus the paper texture, lineC ink at 0.5 on the top edge, and a wet sheen line.
- The foot band is a vertical gradient (lcfoot), opaque to bankY+1.6 and fading to nothing at bankY+3.8. It is laid over the land's top edge, clipped to the land paths, with its opacity scaled by exposure.
- The wrack is short pale strokes at the feet on its own mulberry(6611) seed, so the grass's g() draws are untouched.

Layers: all of it is on #sceneSvg, the still layer. The paint order is now flats, bank mud, palmetto trunks, land, foot band and wrack, then the oak's back. Swapping the palm trunks to after the flats changes no pixels, because the two never overlap. The tufts stay on #sceneFx with their sway unchanged and only gain a data-grass attribute. No animation, transform or filter was added, and PRM gives 0 animations. Measuring tags data-ground="water|mud|land" were added to the river rect, the flats, the bank mud and the land.

The check: grassCheck in tools/beaufort/scene.mjs runs on every case at every width. It reads each foot from the blade paths and classifies the point under it by the topmost data-ground shape there (isPointInFill, mapped through getScreenCTM). It does this at the case's own tide, then repaints at 0, .15, .5, .8 and 1 by swapping in tideLevel and calling render(LAST...), awaiting PAINT each time. A foot fails if it is over air, over water below 0.94, or, at or below mean tide, has open water within 1.5 units above it (rising to 2.5 at dead low). PORCH_BFT_GRASS_TIDES overrides the sweep tides.

selfReview:
- It is a storybook fix, not optics. The exposed mud shows as a band rising above each bank's top line (standing in for the river-side bank and flats beyond the grass), plus a dark band laid over the top of the green. So at low water the green bank's visible edge sits 3 to 6 units lower than at high water. That shift only exists because the spring-high picture had to stay exactly as approved.
- At dead low on the left bank the dark mud is about 10 units (about 12 CSS px at 390). I think it reads right, but it is a heavier dark stripe than before, and Josh may want it thinner or lighter. BFT_GRASS_MUD and the lcfoot stops are the knobs.
- The land's own top ink line stays visible as a faint crease inside the mud at low water, because the foot band is clipped to the land and covers only half of that line. Fine at phone size, visible in close-ups.
- The wrack is effectively invisible on a phone. It only shows in close-ups.
- At night the waterline sheen is a thin pale line, like the flats' wet edges.
- Each corner's mud shoulder hides 6 to 9 units of the flat's top-line ink next to the bank. That slightly changes the flats' silhouette right at the bank. It was deliberate, so the corner grass has ground under it on the flood, and the rest of the flats are byte-identical apart from a tag.
- The check's thresholds (open water must be at least 1.5 units above the foot at mean tide, 2.5 at dead low) are numbers I chose to mean "the foot is seen against mud". Near the corners at mean tide they pass with about 0.5 to 1 unit to spare, so shrinking BFT_GRASS_MUD below about 3 would trip them, by design. The check measures the tufts at rest. Their sway shifts the feet by under 0.1 unit, which it ignores.
- The data-ground and data-grass attributes, about 130 bytes, ship in the live page purely so the harness can measure.
- Merge risks with feature/bft-oak-glow:
  - sw.js and test.mjs line 37: both branches likely bump CACHE to v101, so whichever merges second should take v102 and update that assertion.
  - #sceneSvg template in lowcountryScene: I added `${grassFoot}${wrackSvg}` on the line just before `<g data-prop="live-oak">${oakBack}</g>` and reordered the flats and palmetto trunks, so a text conflict there is possible if the oak branch edits nearby.
